Traditional support lookup tasks are conversational and fact-specific. They are performed through natural language queries targeting specific policies, procedures, or troubleshooting steps—such as asking for a reimbursement limit or resolution steps for a SCIM sync failure [NL-028#NL-028-S06]. These tasks aim to help customer-facing teams and warehouse staff retrieve accurate training and compliance information [NL-023#NL-023-S02]. The core operational concerns involve practical lookup pain points: how long a lookup takes while a customer is on hold, and the cost when a support agent misquotes a policy or pricing tier [NL-009#NL-009-S03].

In contrast, structured BI-style questions are analytical and aggregate. They are processed programmatically via SQL against telemetry tables (e.g., `support_tickets`) to compute sums, averages, and category groupings—such as `SUM(ticket_count)` grouped by category, or `AVG(csat_score)` grouped by plan tier—to track support efficiency trends QoQ and identify SLA bottlenecks like open Severity 1/2 tickets older than 48 hours [NL-029#NL-029-S07].

Therefore, traditional support lookup centers on retrieving a specific grounded fact to serve a customer or employee, while structured BI-style questions center on running analytical aggregations over support data to uncover trends, averages, or operational bottlenecks [NL-028#NL-028-S06] [NL-029#NL-029-S07].
